How DUI Driving Can Affect a Car Accident Claim in Texas

Image Source: Magnific.com

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:52
Instaread

A car accident involving a driver under the influence can make an injury claim more complicated. Alcohol or drug impairment may affect how fault is determined and how the accident is investigated. It can also influence the evidence available to support a victim’s claim.

When a driver chooses to operate a vehicle while impaired, their actions may become important when determining responsibility for a crash. Police reports, test results, witness statements, and other evidence can help show whether intoxication contributed to the collision.

Texas drivers injured in DUI accidents may be able to pursue compensation for losses caused by another driver’s actions. However, the outcome depends on the circumstances of the crash and the evidence available. Understanding how DUI driving affects a claim can help victims know what to expect.

DUI Can Affect How Fault Is Determined

Proving who caused an accident is important for an injury claim. If the driver was impaired, evidence of intoxication may support the claim. Investigators may also examine the driver’s judgment, speed, and ability to control the vehicle.

A DUI charge or arrest does not automatically guarantee compensation. The injured person still needs to establish that the other driver’s conduct caused the accident and resulting injuries. Evidence from the crash can help connect the driver’s behavior to the harm suffered.

Evidence Can Play an Important Role

DUI-related crashes may produce several types of evidence that can become relevant to a civil claim. Police reports, breath or blood testing, field sobriety observations, witness accounts, and traffic-camera footage may help establish what happened.

Medical records are also important when seeking compensation for injuries. They can document the nature of the injuries, treatment received, and ongoing medical needs after the collision.

Keeping accident-related records organized can make it easier to demonstrate the losses caused by the crash.

Insurance Claims May Become More Complicated

After a DUI crash, the victim may need to deal with the impaired driver’s insurance company. An insurer may investigate the accident carefully before deciding whether and how much compensation should be offered. Evidence of alcohol or drug use may also affect the claim.

Insurance companies may also question the extent of injuries or the value of a claim. Providing medical documentation, repair records, and other supporting evidence can help establish the financial impact of the accident.

Victims should avoid assuming that an initial settlement offer represents the full value of their losses.

Texas Shared-Fault Rules Can Still Apply

DUI driving does not necessarily mean the other driver bears every percentage of responsibility for a collision. Texas uses comparative responsibility rules, meaning an injured person’s own actions may also be considered when determining compensation.

This makes the circumstances surrounding the entire accident important. Evidence should establish not only that the other driver was impaired but also how that impairment contributed to the collision.

A complete review of the accident can help clarify the parties’ respective responsibilities.

Compensation May Cover Different Losses

A successful car accident claim may include compensation for losses resulting from the collision. Depending on the circumstances, these can include medical expenses, lost wages, property damage, and pain and suffering.

The amount of compensation depends on the injuries, financial losses, available evidence, and other factors. DUI involvement alone does not guarantee a larger settlement. Each claim must be evaluated based on its specific circumstances.

Key Takeaways

  • DUI evidence can affect how fault is established.
  • Police and medical records may support the claim.
  • Insurance companies may closely investigate DUI-related crashes.
  • Texas comparative responsibility rules can affect compensation.
  • Victims may seek compensation for accident-related losses.
  • DUI involvement does not automatically guarantee a larger settlement.
